17 An object of mass 0.40 kg is projected into the air and follows a curved path above horizontal ground.

path of object
ground
18 m
object, mass 0.40 kg

The object takes a time of 1.5 s to move along its path. The object lands a horizontal distance of 18 m from its initial position. Air resistance is negligible.

What is the kinetic energy of the object at its maximum height?
A 0 J
B 2.4 J
C 11 J
D 29 J

hints: Notice the diagram shows an $18 \text{ m}$ horizontal range covered in a flight time of $1.5 \text{ s}$ with negligible air resistance.
Connect that horizontal motion to constant horizontal velocity, since there is no horizontal acceleration without air resistance.
Remember that at maximum height the vertical velocity is zero, so the kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ depends only on the horizontal speed you found.
walkthrough: Identify the horizontal information: range $= 18 \text{ m}$ and time of flight $= 1.5 \text{ s}$, with mass $m = 0.40 \text{ kg}$.
Because air resistance is negligible, horizontal velocity $v_x$ is constant, so $v_x = \frac{\text{horizontal displacement}}{\text{time}} = \frac{18}{1.5} = 12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
At maximum height the vertical component of velocity $v_y = 0$, but the object still moves horizontally with $v = v_x = 12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Use kinetic energy $E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ with only this speed: $E_k = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.40 \times 12^2$.
Calculate $12^2 = 144$, then $E_k = 0.20 \times 144 = 28.8 \text{ J}$, about $29 \text{ J}$ with correct units of joules. This is option D.

A.explanation: The total velocity is not zero at maximum height because the horizontal component remains. Only the vertical component is momentarily zero.

B.explanation: This is far too small and comes from confusing horizontal distance with a vertical energy change. The sustained horizontal motion of $18 \text{ m}$ in $1.5 \text{ s}$ gives a much larger speed.

C.explanation: This would correspond to using about half the horizontal speed. The full horizontal speed from $18 \text{ m}$ divided by $1.5 \text{ s}$ must be used in $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$.

D.explanation: Horizontal speed is $12 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and this is the only speed at maximum height, giving $\frac{1}{2} \times 0.40 \times 12^2 \approx 29 \text{ J}$.
